standard.title: Analyse and evaluate information in texts
standard.description: analyse and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written and multimodal texts and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret and analyse texts with cultural and critical awareness, evaluate source credibility, and respond with empathy and critical stance (AC9LCH8C03). They have analysed register, humour and cultural reference. They have not yet evaluated texts using formal analytical frameworks, used public speaking and debating strategies, accessed formal text types such as official policies, or referenced sources in target language academic contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate information, ideas and perspectives in a broad range of spoken, written and multimodal texts — including formal text types, literary extracts, and public discourse — responding appropriately using public speaking, debating or analytical writing strategies.

nodes.label: Evaluating formal and policy texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can access and evaluate formal text types — policies, procedures, official documents, news — assessing their validity, reliability and credibility, and citing sources in target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least two formal target language texts for validity, reliability and credibility using explicit criteria, and cite at least one source appropriately in target language.
nodes.typical_width: Access formal text types — emergency procedures, policies, news, academic resources; evaluate validity, reliability and credibility; gather and cite references in target language; use formal analytical language to discuss and evaluate; compare formal target language sources with English equivalents.
wider: Conduct a research task using formal target language sources — evaluate source quality, synthesise across sources, and present findings with citations in target language
Compare how credibility is signalled differently in target language and English formal texts — identify differences in citation conventions, author authority markers, and evidence presentation
nodes.hinge_reason: Formal text evaluation with citation is the prerequisite for all analytical and academic response work at Y9-10. Students who cannot evaluate formal sources or cite them appropriately cannot produce the evaluative, evidence-based responses the descriptor and creating strand require.

response_modes.reason: Formal text evaluation and citation require explicit instruction on the criteria and conventions — these are not intuitive. Explicit instruction on formal source evaluation frameworks and target language citation conventions, followed by guided practice, builds the academic literacy capacity needed.

success_criteria: Evaluates at least two formal texts using explicit credibility criteria
Cites at least one source appropriately in target language

nodes.label: Public speaking and debating strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use public speaking, debating and interview strategies to respond to a variety of text types and topics, evaluating peers' performances and demonstrating cultural knowledge.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one structured public speaking or debating task in target language, using at least two formal oral communication strategies appropriate to the format.
nodes.typical_width: Use public speaking, debating and interview strategies to respond to texts and topics; analyse key elements of successful interviews and speeches; simulate formal oral communication contexts; evaluate peers' performances; role-play modified scenes from target language media demonstrating cultural knowledge.
wider: Prepare and deliver a formal speech or debate contribution on an issue of significance — evaluate own performance against identified criteria and revise for a second delivery
Analyse a published target language speech or interview — identify the specific strategies used and explain how each serves the communicative purpose

response_modes.reason: Public speaking and debating require repeated performance practice with feedback — these are skills built through doing, not only preparation. Regular structured oral performance tasks with peer and self-evaluation build the confidence and strategic capability the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Public speaking in the target language is a high-visibility marker of background learner achievement. Width investment here — particularly in debate and formal speech tasks on issues of genuine relevance — develops the confidence and capability that makes target language use personally meaningful.
success_criteria: Participates in a structured public speaking or debating task using at least two formal oral strategies
Demonstrates cultural knowledge relevant to the topic or context

nodes.label: Responding to literary and cultural texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read and respond to literary and cultural texts — including traditional literature and culturally significant works — with analytical and personal depth.
nodes.minimum_width: Read an extract from a target language literary or cultural text and produce a reflective response of at least eight sentences, with at least two analytical observations about the text.
nodes.typical_width: Read extracts from traditional target language literature — plays, poems, novels, prose; analyse plots, characters and cultural knowledge; write and perform reflective personal responses; create or extend literary texts; keep reading journals; write reflective responses to First Nations Australian stories in target language.
wider: Compare a traditional target language literary text with a contemporary work on a similar theme — identify how cultural values and literary conventions have or have not changed
Produce a reflective literary response that situates the text in its cultural and historical context, drawing on background research

response_modes.reason: Literary response integrates formal text evaluation (node 1) and oral performance skills (node 2) into the full analytical and interpretive demand of this descriptor. The teaching investment is in creating genuine engagement with literary texts — real reading, real personal response — rather than only analytical exercise.

success_criteria: Produces a reflective response to a literary or cultural text of at least eight sentences
Includes at least two analytical observations about the text's language, structure or cultural context
